note.explanation: In a laboratory emergency, stay calm, warn people to evacuate, and follow the correct safety steps. For a fire, close doors to confine it and use a fire extinguisher if it is safe to do so. Call and assist emergency staff.
examples: For a fire: alert people, evacuate, close doors to confine the fire, use a fire extinguisher if safe, and call emergency staff.
For a chemical emergency: follow the safety procedures for that chemical and call emergency staff.
note.checkAnswer: Stay calm, alert people to evacuate, close doors to confine the fire, use a fire extinguisher if safe, and call emergency staff.
note.simple: Stay calm. Warn people. Get everyone to safety. Follow the right procedure and call for help.
note.checkQuestion: Name two actions to take during a laboratory emergency.
note.title: Handling a Laboratory Emergency
steps: Stay calm and do not panic.
Alert people in the area to evacuate.
In case of fire, close doors to confine fire. Use fire extinguisher to put down the fire.
In case of chemical emergency adopt safety procedures as mentioned in article 13.1.
note.answer: Stay calm, alert people to evacuate, follow the correct fire or chemical safety procedure, and call emergency staff.

written.text: A few decades ago, a tanker carrying poisonous chlorine gas leaked and the gas spread over a large area in Lahore. The accident killed a few persons as well as animals. Give some concrete proposals to avoid such an accident in future.
written.finalAnswer: Use warning signs to identify poisonous chemicals, handle and transport them with care, follow safety instructions strictly, ensure trained people know the emergency procedures, and hold drills so emergency equipment and responses are checked.

rubric.why: Signs and symbols communicate the hazardous nature of chemicals.

rubric.why: Checking equipment helps ensure it can be used in an emergency.

modelAnswer: Use warning signs and symbols so people know that chlorine is poisonous and hazardous.
Handle and transport the chemical with care and follow safety instructions strictly.
Ensure the people responsible know the emergency procedures and can call emergency staff.
Hold periodic drills to practise the response to a leak.
Check that emergency equipment is in proper working order.

Answer: Use warning signs to identify poisonous chemicals, handle and transport them with care, follow safety instructions strictly, ensure trained people know the emergency procedures, and hold drills so emergency equipment and responses are checked.

examTips: This section may be tested as short answers about emergency drills, evacuation, fire response, signs and symbols, and chemical hazards.
For a fire-response answer, give the actions in a clear order: stay calm, alert people to evacuate, close doors to confine the fire, use a fire extinguisher, and call emergency staff.
For a longer answer, include several separate safety measures rather than repeating the same idea.
For emergency drills, earn marks by mentioning both practical preparation and checking that firefighting equipment works properly.
